learningObjective: Compare how two equal parameters with different gradient-history scales receive unequal coupled L2 shrinkage in Adam but equal direct shrinkage in AdamW.
mediumRationale: An original, phone-width explanatory drawing keeps the complete comparison visible without panning. A topic-specific timeline, quantity, evidence gate, or state relation replaces the component inventory. Geometry, direct labels, accessible descriptions, theme tokens, and static output carry the explanation without interaction.

pages.insight: The preceding optimization slide introduces movement through parameter space and gradient descent, establishing the local-update context for the optimizer equations that follow.
The deck places SGD, momentum, RMSProp, and Adam update equations side by side and explicitly divides each Adam update by the square root of its per-parameter second-moment estimate.
The neighboring RAdam slide emphasizes that early second-moment variance changes Adam's effective step size and motivates warmup; it does not discuss weight decay.
The loss-functions slide describes L2 regularization as discouraging large weights, but does not connect the penalty to adaptive optimizer scaling.
The model-training checklist recommends increasing weight decay as an overfitting control, without distinguishing coupled L2 regularization from decoupled decay.

deckReview.notes: The complete 214-page deck was text-indexed for optimizer, Adam, regularization, L2, and weight-decay material. Every match was reviewed, with visual inspection of the optimizer sequence on pages 45-48. Page 46 directly supports per-parameter adaptive scaling; pages 45 and 47 supply neighboring context, while page 48 moves to SAM. Pages 36 and 62 mention L2 regularization and weight decay only generically. No slide explains AdamW or decoupled weight decay, so the visual does not reuse deck artwork.

sources.title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization
sources.usage: Used to verify Proposition 2 and the fixed-preconditioner intuition: coupled L2 regularization is scaled coordinate-wise, while decoupled weight decay applies one rate.

sourceReview.notes: The table is an original worked example derived from the cited update rules. It explicitly holds the preconditioner fixed to isolate the regularization contribution and does not claim to reproduce a paper experiment.

agentReview.summary: Independently reviewed the complete article, deck, primary papers, and official framework documentation. The hardest prose-only model is why equal parameters can receive different regularization under adaptive scaling, so the final design rejects a generic loss surface in favor of one fixed-preconditioner comparison.

implementation.accessibility: With theta one, alpha .01, lambda .1, and fixed adaptive scales one and ten, coupled L2 contributes shrinkage .001 and .0001. AdamW contributes equal .001 shrinkage. Leftward arrows share the same parameter-distance scale; this isolates the penalty and is not a full Adam recurrence. All labels use at least 12 viewBox units in a 360-unit-wide composition. Meaning is also encoded by positions, words, line styles, and numbers, not color alone.
